message.text: When Melian's install, or the instrumenter's, is unidentified, `reusable` is false. `runLenses` then refuses to attach even to the live lens task that this same review started on this same install and that a crash interrupted. `own` creates a new LensTask and `abortTask`s the old one, so every lens starts again from zero. The head decision states this as its own rule ("It then neither attaches to the stored task nor copies a lens run"). Its `Amends:` lines name lens-runs-reused-per-request, the instrumenter decision and the two code-version decisions. They do not name Review attachment, which is ACTIVE at base and says "a repeat call attaches, never duplicates" because "A crash must not double the model spend". The only amendment at base, lens-runs-reused-per-request, relaxes that rule only "for a selection whose lens requests differ". Here the requests are identical.

evidence.snippet:
Choice: One lens task per head, and one adjudication task per head and input, recorded in a root index; a repeat call attaches, never duplicates, and an adjudication the index no longer names records no verdict

Why: A crash must not double the model spend, nor let an older verdict overwrite a newer one

# Request keys hold Melian's whole install

Amends: [A producer's code version comes from recorded module hashes](2026-11-18-code-versions-from-recorded-hashes.md), "How it is built" and "What it gives up", whose sentences that installed packages are left out, since the lockfile pins them, this replaces

Amends: [The checks' code version comes from recorded module hashes](2026-11-20-check-code-from-recorded-hashes.md), "The change", which now holds Melian's install beside the checks' code

Amends: [A lens run offered `list_mutants` keys the instrumenter that answers it](2026-11-16-lens-request-keys-the-mutant-instrumenter.md), whose key held the instrumenter's version but not the install it runs from

Amends: [A lens run is reused by its request key, one lens at a time](2026-11-15-lens-runs-reused-per-request.md), whose key held the versions of Pi Durable and pi-ai alone

2. **Lenses.** `runLenses` takes `reusable`, false when Melian's install or the instrumenter's is unidentified. It then neither attaches to the stored task nor copies a lens run from another. The lens request holds `identified` beside `packages`, so a review on an identified install never attaches to a run made on an unidentified one with the same digest, which the review of record found the gate alone allowed. Tests in `lens-reuse-review.test.ts`: the second review asks every lens again, and copies none, whichever of the two installs is unidentified.

explanation.what: When Melian's install, or the instrumenter's, is unidentified, `reusable` is false. `runLenses` then refuses to attach even to the live lens task that this same review started on this same install and that a crash interrupted. `own` creates a new LensTask and `abortTask`s the old one, so every lens starts again from zero. The head decision states this as its own rule ("It then neither attaches to the stored task nor copies a lens run"). Its `Amends:` lines name lens-runs-reused-per-request, the instrumenter decision and the two code-version decisions. They do not name Review attachment, which is ACTIVE at base and says "a repeat call attaches, never duplicates" because "A crash must not double the model spend". The only amendment at base, lens-runs-reused-per-request, relaxes that rule only "for a selection whose lens requests differ". Here the requests are identical.
explanation.whatToDo: Either declare the amendment of Review attachment, so the maintainer rules on the extra spend, or keep live-task attachment on an unidentified install. For example, let a review attach to a non-terminal lens task its own install created. You could record a per-process or per-store install marker in the task input that the identity rules allow. Or limit the `reusable` gate to copying finished runs and attaching to finished tasks.
explanation.whyHere: The head text sets its own standard for a behaviour an active base decision governs, without declaring the conflict. The reason the base decision exists, that a crash must not double model spend, is broken for every review on an unidentified install. The gate is there to stop one install standing in for another install with the same digest. But a crash-resume on the same host, with the same install and the same store, is not that case, and it is refused anyway.

properties.failureScenario: A developer's Melian install is unidentified. For example, they ran `npm link yaml` in Melian's install, so `node_modules/yaml` links outside it (doctor warns "links outside Melian's install"). Or Melian is installed under Yarn Plug'n'Play, with `.pnp.cjs` above the module. They run `melian review` and the lens task starts its conversations. The process is then killed partway (Ctrl-C, OOM, or the laptop sleeping and the terminal closing). They run `melian review` again, as the recovery says. At base, `own` would find the index entry with the same selection and attach to the live task, which resumes its conversations, so the turns already paid for are kept. At head, `reusable` is false (review.ts 3386-3387), so `attach` is false (1857-1863). `copiesFrom` is skipped, a new LensTask is created, and `replaced` is aborted (1919-1921). Every lens is asked again from its first turn, so the model spend before the crash is paid twice, about $5 a full round by the decision's own figure. This repeats on every interrupted review for as long as the install stays unidentified.

message.text: `#follow` gives an exemption to every link whose real target is beneath the install root. Such a link is not marked `links outside`, so the install stays identified, and only the target's `package.json` is keyed, not its files. The comment and the decision justify this as "a workspace package's source is no release; the code version covers it". But the class is decided by `#beneath(target)`, and the root is "the outermost ancestor of the module that holds a node_modules" (Install.read lines 49-50). So the exemption covers any directory under that ancestor, not just Melian's workspace packages. A stray `~/node_modules` above a checkout makes the root the home directory. An `npm link` target such as `~/work/yaml` then counts as "inside the install" and is treated as a workspace package that no code version covers. The same holds for a `file:./vendor/x` dependency npm links inside the checkout.

evidence.snippet:
- The install root is the outermost ancestor of the module that holds a `node_modules`, since Node searches every ancestor's.
- In a `node_modules` directory, each child is a package slot, and an `@scope` child holds slots. A name starting with a dot, such as `.bin` or `.cache`, is walked as a plain tree.
- A package records `[place, "manifest", digest]`, a SHA-256 of its `package.json`'s bytes, or `[place, "no manifest"]`, since Node can load one. The whole manifest is keyed, not its name and version alone, because `exports`, `main` and `type` change what runs at one version. The digest is over the file's bytes, not core's `canonicalJson`, which refuses a fraction or a lone surrogate that a manifest may hold. Melian does not parse it: Node strips a byte-order mark that `JSON.parse` refuses, so a parse would fail a manifest Node loads, as the review of record found. Its subdirectories are walked for a nested `node_modules`.
- A link records `[place, "links", target]`, and is never walked through. A target beneath the root is walked where it really is, with each `node_modules` on its ancestor chain up to the root, since Node resolves the target's imports from there. A linked package records its target's manifest but not its other files, since a workspace package's source is no release; the code version covers it.

A link out of the install, such as `npm link yaml` to `/work/yaml`, names a place the walk cannot read without walking the host. It records the fixed entry `["node_modules/yaml", "links outside"]`, adds the place to `outside`, and walks no further. The digest stays deterministic, and `identified` reads false. No value drawn at random enters any key, so rule 6 of [the identity guideline](../guidelines/identity.md#rules) stands as written, and this decision amends nothing there.

explanation.what: `#follow` gives an exemption to every link whose real target is beneath the install root. Such a link is not marked `links outside`, so the install stays identified, and only the target's `package.json` is keyed, not its files. The comment and the decision justify this as "a workspace package's source is no release; the code version covers it". But the class is decided by `#beneath(target)`, and the root is "the outermost ancestor of the module that holds a node_modules" (Install.read lines 49-50). So the exemption covers any directory under that ancestor, not just Melian's workspace packages. A stray `~/node_modules` above a checkout makes the root the home directory. An `npm link` target such as `~/work/yaml` then counts as "inside the install" and is treated as a workspace package that no code version covers. The same holds for a `file:./vendor/x` dependency npm links inside the checkout.
explanation.whatToDo: Grant the manifest-only exemption only to link targets the code version actually covers: Melian's own workspace packages, named by the workspaces of the package that holds the module, or the paths `code-hashes.ts` records. Treat any other link to a package directory like a link outside: record a fixed entry and leave the install unidentified. Or key its files.
explanation.whyHere: The decision says a link out of the install, "such as `npm link yaml` to `/work/yaml`", leaves the install unidentified so that no run is reused. The code gives that guarantee only when no ancestor of the checkout holds a `node_modules`. When one does, the linked package's code is edited freely under an unchanged digest that reads identified. Check runs, lens runs and adjudications made under the old code are then reused.

properties.failureScenario: A developer has a Melian checkout at `/home/u/src/melian` and a stray `/home/u/node_modules`, left by an `npm install` run once in their home directory. They run `npm link yaml` against a local fork at `/home/u/work/yaml`, so `realpathSync(node_modules/yaml)` is `/home/u/work/yaml`. `Install.read` takes the chain [`/home/u/src/melian`, `/home/u`], so the root is `/home/u` (lines 49-50). `#follow` finds the target beneath the root. It records `["src/melian/node_modules/yaml","links","work/yaml"]` and the fork's manifest digest, pushes nothing to `outside`, and `identified` is true. The developer then edits `/home/u/work/yaml/dist/compose.js`, which changes how `melian.yaml` is parsed, and runs `melian review` on the same head. `melianInstall().digest` is unchanged and identified, so `checkReusable` passes and `runChecks` reuses the guardrails run the old parser decided. `runLenses` also attaches to or copies the earlier lens runs. Doctor prints "nothing in Melian's install links outside it". Without the stray `~/node_modules`, the same link reads `links outside` and nothing is reused, as the decision promises at line 79. A `"yaml": "file:./vendor/yaml"` dependency inside the checkout behaves the same with no stray directory at all.
